scope: Existing Gmail recovery timeouts; no connections, credentials or mailbox actions performed.
observations: The same immutable bf38 executable timed out under its 45-second outer deadline and later completed in 6676 ms.
Recovery exercises at least five separate IMAP TLS sessions and an SMTP authentication/QUIT probe.
The 45-second aggregate deadline is shorter than the core 60-second per-command timeout and can cancel a slow operation before its own diagnostic timeout.
Remote-search stage includes connection, authentication, LIST, SELECT, exact search, optional metadata/snippet fetch and publication.
Second hydration repeats selective fetching to establish persisted Reader cache behavior.
conclusion: No deterministic product correctness bug or exact timeout cause was demonstrated. A passing direct Python search is not equivalent to the complete Dakia path.
nextDiagnostic: Add nonsecret elapsed timings for IMAP probe, SMTP probe, header sync, search, first Reader fetch, cache-producing hydration and cache read before one further read-only recovery. Do not resend.
limitations: This is source investigation, not another provider acceptance run.
The extra sessions and deadline mismatch may affect latency but are not proven causes of the recorded timeouts.
